jobs.title: Vice President, Advisor Consultant
jobs.description:
The Vice President, Advisor Consultant is a key external-facing sales position within Antares’ Wealth Distribution team, responsible for driving strategic growth across the assigned territory region. through deep engagement with financial intermediaries, including wirehouses, registered investment advisors, and independent broker-dealers.

This role serves as a critical conduit between Antares’ investment platform and the advisor community, ensuring that the firm’s alternative investment offerings, particularly in private credit and direct lending are well positioned, understood, and adopted across key distribution channels. This position is not just about sales, it’s about strategic influence, market leadership, and enterprise growth. The VP, Advisor Consultant, is instrumental in translating Antares’ investment excellence into advisor adoption and client outcomes, making it a cornerstone role in the firm’s long-term distribution strategy.

Responsibilities
- The Vice President,  Alternative Investment Regional Director is responsible for the execution of all sales, service, and marketing related activities in their region within registered Investment advisors, wirehouses and independent broker dealer channels for products including both perpetual and drawdown style alternative investment funds
- Directly manage major markets within their region with a client-centric, sales driven approach to the marketplace
- Develop territory business plans and act as a key point of contact for financial advisors within your market to provide insights and solutions
- Develop and execute a regional sales strategy consistent with the National sales goals with accountability for the overall performance of the region
- Implement territory business plans, generate leads, and actively seek new business opportunities within the region
- Effectively manage the assigned territory, including tracking sales performance, identifying trends, and implementing strategies to improve results
- Convey deep technical knowledge of the firm’s investment strategies and fund vehicles
- Work effectively in a collaborative team environment by maintaining open communication with internal teams and external partners, providing timely updates and solutions to challenges

Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in finance or a related area (MBA, CFA, CAIA or equivalent strongly preferred)

- A demonstrated history of sales performance in an account management position and client relationships across wire‐houses, broker dealers, and RIA partners
- A knowledge of alternative investment products and services, including BDCs. (Private credit and direct
lending preferred, or other alternative credit strategies)
- Ability to work collaboratively and can balance a variety of diverse stakeholders
- Consistent in delivering high quality work in a demanding environment
- Ability to clearly articulate viewpoints verbally and in writing, fostering confidence when sharing and
presenting information
- Proven ability to develop and execute sales strategies across multiple distribution channels (wirehouses, RIAs preferred)
- Strong track record of meeting or exceeding sales targets in complex financial environments.

Core Competencies
- Ability to influence platform placement and product adoption through trust and credibility.
- Ability to translate complex investment strategies into compelling value propositions.
- Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present to both internal stakeholders and external clients.
- Works effectively across marketing, product, and operations to align sales efforts with broader business goals.
- Demonstrates a collaborative mindset and ability to manage diverse stakeholder interests.
- Proactive, forward-thinking approach to identifying and solving challenges in a dynamic environment.
- Comfortable navigating ambiguity and driving initiatives with limited oversight.
- Demonstrates alignment with Antares’ core values: accountability, collaboration, transparency, and empowerment.

The Fine Print
- Must have unrestricted authorization to work in the United States.
- Must be willing to comply with pre-employment screening, including but not limited to drug testing, reference verification, and background check.
- Must be willing to work from the New York office.

Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

jobs.title: Vice President, Front Office Program Manager - Asset Management
jobs.description:
The Asset Management Platforms & Data Services team is a critical part of Antares, partnering across the organization to deliver technology, data and operational capabilities that support investment, investor and business processes.

The Vice President, Front Office Asset Management Program Manager is a senior leadership role responsible for driving complex, cross-functional transformation and strategic initiatives across business, technology and data. Reporting to the SVP, Group Lead, Asset Management Platforms & Data Services, this individual operates at the intersection of front office investment teams and the technology and data organization — serving both equally and credibly. The role requires a strong, hands-on operator who can move comfortably between strategy and execution, bring structure to ambiguous problems, mobilize multidisciplinary teams, drive decisions and dependencies, and maintain momentum through delivery. This individual will partner closely with portfolio management, investment operations, and business technology leaders to translate strategic priorities into coordinated execution, adoption, and measurable business outcomes. The role will also leverage AI-enabled approaches, automation, and emerging technologies to accelerate execution and scale organizational capacity. The VP will lead emerging strategic priorities that require horizontal leadership across organizational boundaries.

Responsibilities

- Lead complex, cross-functional transformation and strategic initiatives from initial problem framing through implementation, adoption and measurable outcomes.
- Translate strategic objectives into executable plans with clear priorities, sequencing, milestones, dependencies, decision points and accountable owners.
- Mobilize and lead integrated business and technology teams around defined outcomes, establishing effective operating cadences and clear accountability.
- Coordinate execution across business stakeholders, technology, data, architecture, data governance, quality and other enterprise capabilities while preserving functional ownership.
- Identify and resolve cross-functional dependencies, risks and execution barriers; elevate decisions requiring senior leadership intervention with clear options and recommendations.
- Partner with initiative leaders to define success measures and appropriate baselines, and drive accountability for delivery, adoption, value realization and measurable business outcomes.
- Identify and apply AI-enabled approaches, automation, and emerging technologies to accelerate delivery, scale organizational capacity, and establish repeatable practices that improve business processes and outcomes.
- Drive effective coordination across internal teams and strategic delivery partners, ensuring resources are aligned to priorities and outcomes.
- Provide concise, decision-oriented communications to senior stakeholders on progress, risks, dependencies, outcomes and required actions.
- Lead emerging strategic initiatives that require cross-functional coordination, problem solving, judgment and execution leadership.

Qualifications

The successful candidate will bring a demonstrated track record of personally driving complex initiatives from strategy through execution and measurable business outcomes. This role requires more than transformation oversight or program governance; candidates should be able to demonstrate where they have taken ownership, worked through execution challenges and delivered tangible value to the organization.

Required:

- Bachelor's degree in business, finance, technology, engineering, data or a related field.
- 10+ years of relevant experience, including significant experience leading complex technology, data, operating model or business transformation initiatives.
- Demonstrated success personally leading cross-functional initiatives across organizational boundaries and influencing stakeholders from problem definition through implementation, adoption and measurable value realization without relying solely on direct reporting authority.
- Strong business acumen with the ability to connect technology and data investments to business objectives and measurable outcomes.
- Exceptional communication skills — written, verbal, and executive presence — with demonstrated ability to translate complex, multi-dimensional issues into clear narratives, decisions, and actions tailored to C-suite, business, and technical audiences.
- Demonstrated experience applying AI, automation or emerging technologies to improve business processes, accelerate delivery or create measurable organizational value.
- Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and coordinating internal and external delivery partners.
- Experience within private markets, private credit, alternative asset management or a closely related investment-management environment.
- Demonstrated ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy — setting direction, managing competing priorities, and driving initiatives forward without requiring close supervision or frequent escalation for routine decisions.

Preferred:

- Experience with enterprise data, analytics, workflow, technology platforms or technology-enabled operating-model transformation.
- Experience in management consulting, technology consulting, internal strategy/transformation, or a comparable role requiring a highly consultative approach to solving complex business problems.
- Experience and background in buy-side financial technology industry.
- Prior experience supporting, partnering with, or embedded within a buy-side portfolio management, investment operations, or front office team not just working adjacent to one.
- Advanced degree or relevant professional certification.

Skills

This role requires combination of strategic thinking and hands-on execution capability. The successful candidate must be equally comfortable framing an executive-level problem, working through the underlying details with delivery teams, and personally driving the actions required to move an initiative forward.

- Strong analytical, problem-structuring and agile problem-solving skills; able to quickly frame ambiguous issues, test assumptions, adapt as new information emerges and translate problems into executable paths forward.
- Strong practical fluency with AI-enabled tools and approaches, including the ability to identify opportunities to augment individual and team capacity, accelerate problem solving and embed AI into the scalable business and delivery processes.
- Technology and data fluency sufficient to operate credibly across engineering, architecture, data, analytics, workflow and platform teams.
- Hands-on execution orientation with the ability and willingness to work directly through problems, decisions, and deliverables rather than operating solely through governance or oversight.
- Ability to rapidly learn unfamiliar business and technology domains, identify what matters and translate that understanding into action.
- Strong ability to create momentum – converting ambiguity into structure, structure into decisions and decisions into execution.
- Exceptional stakeholder management, influencing and executive communication skills.
- Strong prioritization, decision-making and execution discipline in complex environments.
- Ability to move fluidly between strategic framing and detailed execution as circumstances require.
- Strong consultative skills, with the ability to understand business needs, challenge assumptions constructively, develop pragmatic solutions and partner with stakeholders through implementation and successful outcomes.
- Ability to connect delivery activity to adoption, business value and measurable outcomes.
- Strong written and verbal communication, including executive-level presentations and decision materials.
- Working knowledge of private credit investment processes, loan lifecycle, and portfolio monitoring workflows sufficient to engage credibly with portfolio management and investment operations teams — and to quickly identify where technology and data can drive meaningful improvements.
- Ability to lead organizational change and manage adoption — including building stakeholder readiness, managing resistance, and sustaining engagement through multi-phase transformation.
- Ability to sustain composure, credibility, and forward momentum in high-pressure, high-ambiguity environments with competing executive priorities — bringing calm, structured thinking when the stakes are highest.

Competencies

The successful candidate will bring a highly proactive, ownership-oriented leadership style with a strong bias towards action and urgency. They will be intellectually curious, proactive in identifying where they can create value, motivated by complex challenges and committed to serving business partners through practical outcomes rather than process for its own sake.

- Leadership: Creates clarity and momentum across multidisciplinary teams and holds stakeholders accountable for shared outcomes.
- Business & Commercial Awareness: Understands business priorities and evaluates transformation opportunities through the lens of value, scalability, risk and operating leverage.
- Judgment & Decision Making: Exercises sound judgment in ambiguous situations, identifies the decisions that matter and drives them to resolution.
- Influence & Collaboration: Builds credibility across functions and levels and can align stakeholders without formal authority.
- Ownership & Accountability: Takes responsibility for outcomes, follows through on commitments and proactively addresses barriers to execution.
- Adaptability & Agility: Moves effectively across different problems, domains and levels of detail; learns quickly, adapts approach as circumstances change and can be deployed against evolving strategic priorities. Maintains steady, composed leadership under pressure — projecting confidence and structure even in ambiguous or fast-moving situations.
- Problem Solving: Synthesizes complex information, challenges assumptions and develops pragmatic solutions.
- Communication: Communicates with clarity, confidence, and precision across executive, business and technical audiences — turning complex, multi-layered topics into compelling narratives that drive understanding and action. Equally effective in a boardroom briefing, a written memo, and a working session with delivery teams.
- Integrity: Demonstrates sound judgment, discretion and high ethical standards — particularly in sensitive, high-stakes situations involving senior leaders, business partners, and confidential information. Earns trust through consistent, principled behavior and transparency.

jobs.title: Vice President, Senior Compliance Manager - Regulatory Counsel
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Compliance team is a critical and strategic function at Antares Capital, playing a central role in enabling the firm’s growth while upholding the highest regulatory and ethical standards. We are seeking a highly motivated, intellectually curious, and driven individual to join our team. This individual will be an integral member of a 7-person Compliance team, reporting directly to the Managing Director, Chief Compliance Officer, and will have meaningful exposure to senior leadership across the firm.

This role offers a unique opportunity to engage deeply across all facets of the compliance program and to contribute as a trusted advisor and subject matter expert. The successful candidate will help advance the firm’s compliance framework by: (1) Providing thoughtful, practical guidance on the application of global regulations, evolving industry developments, and best practices in support of our private credit strategy and fund structures and the general growth of the firm’s asset management transactional activities; (2) Interpreting and operationalizing compliance policies and procedures to align with the firm’s existing and newly developing products and business activities and the firm’s expanding jurisdictional reach; (3) Leading and coordinating the implementation of new regulatory requirements and enhancements to existing frameworks; and (4) Partnering cross-functionally to represent Compliance in enterprise-wide initiatives, while supporting day-to-day matters and broader program oversight.

This position is designed for impact and growth, with a path to expand responsibilities over time, including the potential to evolve into a Deputy CCO role.

Responsibilities
- Assist in the oversight of the firm’s compliance program through development and enhancement of the processes and procedures required to comply and align with all laws, regulatory rules, and relevant firm policies.
- Identify potential areas of compliance vulnerability and risk. Develop and implement corrective action plans for resolution of problematic issues and provide general guidance on how to avoid or deal with similar situations in the future.
- Assist in management of the firm’s compliance risk assessment that focuses on the identification and evaluation of Compliance risks throughout the company.
- Lead and participate in cross-functional teams of internal staff and be responsible for complex projects.

Qualifications
- A minimum of 8-10 years of relevant compliance experience in the asset management industry (private debt experience preferred)
- Law firm, in-house and/or SEC experience a plus,
- JD required
- Active license to practice law
- Proven knowledge and experience in the regulation of registered investment advisers and Business Development Companies. Comprehensive knowledge of US laws applicable to investment advisers, including the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 and Investment Company Act of 1940.
- Ability to identify regulatory and compliance issues, propose solutions and raise significant issues to firm leadership.
- Strong work ethic and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment while also learning.
- Excellent verbal and written communications skills with the ability to understand, simplify and communicate internal and external regulations, risks, laws, and policies in a clear, focused, and concise manner. Ability to tailor communication (verbal and written) to multiple target audiences with different levels of compliance acumen.

Skills
- Ability to influence others via a service-minded orientation, build trust and work cross-functionally within the organization and with outside regulatory bodies.
- Experience with Microsoft Suite including: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook or comparable software application (SharePoint experience preferred, but not required).
- Ability to analyze and evaluate data, forming accurate conclusions and translating insights into action.

Competencies
- Strategic thinking and decision making: Applies strong business and market insight and expertise to shape functional/team strategy, solves complex problems, recommends best practices, makes high quality decisions, anticipates future needs and delivers stakeholder aligned value.
- Drives execution and results: Translates enterprise and functional goals into clear initiatives within their scope. Remove barriers and drives teams or others to deliver timely and high-quality results.
- Cultivates strategic relationships and influence: Builds strong internal and external relationships, understands organizational dynamics to influence stakeholders and communicates with impact to align perspectives and advances functional goals.
- Fosters an inclusive culture and leads teams to achieve excellence: Role models and shapes an inclusive and high performing culture by leading or working across teams and functions, setting clear expectations and developing talent to enable strong organizational performance.
- Demonstrates strong self-awareness, integrity, and a growth mindset, adapts leadership to build trust and influence outcomes, challenges assumptions with courage, mitigates risk responsibly, clearly articulates viewpoints verbally and in writing, and guides others through change with confidence and resilience.
- Innovation: Champions innovation by raising new ideas, leveraging data and technology tools (including, as applicable, artificial intelligence) to improve team/function performance and capability.

The Fine Print

- Must be willing to comply with pre-employment screening, including but not limited to drug testing, reference verification, and background check.

jobs.description:

Reporting to the Managing Director, Financial Planning & Analysis, the Compensation Accountant will be responsible for the financial accounting, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting over new and existing compensation plans (e.g., annual discretionary bonus, restricted unit plan, phantom restricted unit plan, carried interest plan, and other incentive plans). This position will also oversee financial accounting of equity purchases and sales under equity purchase programs, and will work closely with the tax and HR teams on tracking relevant data. The role supports the FP&A team during annual budget processes and monthly forecast updates.
Our ideal candidate is independent, motivated, detail‐orientated and able to analyze data and convey conclusions effectively.

- Access appropriate data from new and existing systems and work across departments to complete reports and assignments.
- Prepare quarterly footnotes and compensation schedules for leadership and Board
- Participate and support activities related to “what if” scenario and sensitivity analyses for new and existing business functions and product lines.
- Work seamlessly with HR and FP&A teams to understand financial trends (actuals vs. budget), perform variance analysis and complete other financial reporting projects.

- Enhance controls and document SOPs around processes

- Experience preparing footnotes and equity roll forwards
- Strong understanding of GAAP and financial controls
- Proficiency in financial systems (e.g., Microsoft Dynamics, OneStream, DFIN, JPM Workplace Solutions)

Skills

jobs.title: Analyst, Institutional Investor Coverage
jobs.description:
Job Description

Antares’ Americas Institutional Business Development team is a critical part of the firm, responsible for driving assets under management (AUM) growth through fundraising and the firm’s relationships with institutional investors.
The Analyst’s primary role is to support senior professionals across the team’s fundraising initiatives, helping to drive AUM growth by supporting business-building activities such as CRM management, meeting preparation and follow-up, and collaboration with partner groups to advance investor due diligence requests.

Responsibilities

- Participate in the preparation of capital raising initiatives, such as submitting prospective investor due diligence requests, coordinating road shows, and preparing meeting briefs.
- Monitor planned deployment activity across the institutional investor community and provide updates for weekly team meetings.
- Regularly update and monitor the CRM to ensure data accuracy.
- Participate in virtual pension fund investment committee meetings and review/upload relevant minutes and materials to internal databases.
- Collaborate with Product, IR, and Marketing professionals to support strategic initiatives.
- Coordinate with partner groups across the organization to obtain and synthesize information from the investment teams, performance, legal, tax, operations, finance, and accounting teams to prepare materials and onboard investment vehicles.

Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in finance or a related area
- Knowledge of or a strong interest in direct lending, leveraged finance, or alternative credit preferred
- Willingness and ability in the future to pass Series SIE, Series 7 and 66
- 1+ years of experience in investment banking, asset management, alternative investments, or a sales-support capacity preferred

Skills

- Highly proficient in Excel, PowerPoint, and Word
- Ability to clearly articulate viewpoint verbally and in writing
- Experience working within a CRM database (e.g., Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics)
- Outstanding attention to detail with strong organizational and problem-solving skills

- Passion for financial markets and knowledge of alternative investment products.
- Ability to collaborate and work effectively in a cross-functional team environment.
- Effective verbal and written communication skills.
- Ability to analyze investor databases and determine proper product positioning.
- Self-starter and comfortable working in a fast-paced, often unpredictable, and deadline-oriented environment.
- Flexibility to adjust to changing circumstances.
- Upholding ethical standards and integrity in all interactions.
- Highly motivated self-starter able to set priorities, multitask, and manage workload to meet aggressive deadlines.
- Takes initiative and works independently while demonstrating strong collaboration.

- Strategic thinking and decision making: - Demonstrates a baseline understanding of team, stakeholder and firm priorities and leverages resources to build appropriate industry expertise
- Applies business understanding and an understanding of team goals to work product to execute tasks using a structured and logical approach and makes quality decisions within established guidelines

- Drives execution and results: - Keeps assigned work progressing by confirming expectations, prioritizing and managing tasks to deadlines and promptly surfacing barriers with possible solutions to ensure timely handoffs to downstream partners

- Cultivates strategic relationships and influence: - Establishes working relationships with peers and stakeholders and demonstrates awareness of those relationships when asking questions, analyzing information, sharing insights and delivering work product

- Fosters an inclusive culture and leads teams to achieve excellence: - Demonstrates inclusive behavior, engages respectfully with others and contributes to positive team culture
- Demonstrates respectful collaboration and inclusive behavior by sharing information openly, supporting team discussions and problem-solving and aligning day-to-day work to shared goals to contribute to positive outcomes

- Masters oneself and demonstrates a growth mindset: - Builds personal effectiveness by responding to feedback and participating in learning opportunities
- Demonstrates subject matter expertise and reliability in delivering results, earning trust from senior leadership, peers and teams
- Takes ownership in challenging situations, provides clear guidance and motivates others by showing a commitment to success
- Serves as a trusted advisor and role model with peers and stakeholders
- Complies with all risk and regulatory requirements across the organization
- Takes ownership over assigned work by adapting habits and maintaining focus under pressure during times of change with support

jobs.description:
Job Description
The Reconciliation Team is a critical part of Antares by ensuring the accuracy of investment data internally across the firm as well as externally with counterparties, fund administrators and investor reporting.

Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, the Senior Analyst’s primary role is to perform daily, monthly, quarterly and periodic reconciliations across multiple accounts, portfolios and internal systems and identify root causes. This role is situated in a fast-paced, high-volume environment where you will be expected to apply your analytical skills and financial expertise to ensure accuracy, efficiency, and compliance in all operations.

Responsibilities
- Perform daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly reconciliations of cash, positions, and accrued income values across multiple portfolios, custodians and fund administrators

- Communicate effectively with internal and external parties to ensure discrepancies are identified correctly, assigned appropriately and resolved in a timely manner

- Provide Standard Operating Procedures training and best practices guidance to team members

- Produce complete, accurate and on time monthly tie-out and sign-off deliverables for assigned reconciliations

- Analyze data on assigned reconciliations for escalation issues, recurring break themes and root cause considerations

- Collaborate with IT and Operations teams to enhance reconciliation tools and automate processes where possible

- Identify areas for process improvements and efficiencies within transaction processing and reconciliation

- Implement best practices to enhance operational workflows and accuracy

Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree, with a preferred concentration in finance, accounting, business, or economics

- 3-5 years of experience with a financial institution and data reconciliation processes

- Strong understanding of Loan Operations with some exposure to Structured Products

jobs.title: Senior Vice President, Insurance Solutions - Product/Business Development
jobs.description:
Job Description

Antares is seeking a senior, client-facing professional to drive growth across its insurance segment. This individual will play a critical role in expanding relationships with insurance clients, increasing AUM, and advancing the firm’s commercial strategy across Life, P&C, Health, and multi-line carriers. This SVP-level role is designed for a commercially oriented leader who combines market expertise, strong client relationships, and strategic execution to deliver measurable business outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Revenue Generation & Client Growth
- Drive new business origination and contribute directly to AUM growth within the insurance channel
- Expand and deepen relationships with existing insurance clients, increasing wallet share and long-term partnerships
- Identify and execute on cross-selling opportunities across products and strategies

Client Coverage & Engagement
- Lead senior-level client engagement, including meetings with C-suite and investment decision-makers
- Serve as a trusted advisor to clients by delivering market insights, portfolio perspectives, and tailored solutions
- Maintain a high level of responsiveness and accountability in meeting client needs

Solutions & Product Strategy
- Partner with investment, product, and distribution teams to develop and position differentiated investment solutions
- Translate client demand and market trends into actionable product and go-to-market strategies
- Support commercialization of new strategies and product innovations
- Market Intelligence & Strategic Execution
- Monitor industry trends, regulatory developments, and competitive dynamics to identify opportunities for growth
- Use market insights and data-driven analysis to inform business strategy and client engagement
- Execute against defined commercial priorities, balancing near-term results with long-term strategic positioning

Cross-Functional Leadership
- Collaborate across teams to align on client strategy, product positioning, and business priorities
- Influence stakeholders and drive alignment to accelerate decision-making and execution
- Operate with an enterprise mindset, ensuring efforts support broader firm objectives

Competencies
- Commercial Impact: Demonstrated ability to drive revenue growth, build pipelines, and deliver measurable AUM expansion
- Strategic Leadership: Translate market insights and business objectives into actionable growth strategies
- Executive Presence: Confidently engage and influence senior stakeholders internally and externally
- Accountability: Set and deliver on performance targets; maintain urgency and follow-through
- Collaboration: Build strong partnerships across teams to enable execution and deliver results
- Innovation & Agility: Identify new opportunities, adapt quickly to market changes, and drive continuous improvement

Qualifications
- Experience covering or working with insurance companies, with a strong understanding of insurer investment needs
- Proven track record of business development, client relationship management, or product commercialization
- Knowledge of private credit and alternative investments strongly preferred
- Strong analytical, strategic thinking, and problem-solving capabilities
- Excellent communication and presentation skills; ability to engage senior audiences
